uncertainty_ledger.note: Every known limitation of this vintage, derived from the index at build time. Read it before citing anything.

entries.statement: 3 of 35 states carry no composite: HKG, SGP, TWN. Water stress is absent and coverage falls to 0.70 against the declared 0.75 threshold. The absence has two distinct causes, published per state as withholding_cause.
entries.effect: Those states cannot be ranked or compared on composite.
entries.remedy: Scoped as permanently out of coverage against Aqueduct 4.0 rather than pending. HKG and SGP carry SOURCE_RESOLUTION: no WSE value exists at source for a catchment of that extent, so no amount of access produces one. TWN carries SOURCE_POLITICAL_COVERAGE: the source's territorial schema does not publish a separate entry. Reopening this requires a different water-stress source with city-territory resolution and its own territorial schema, which would be a new axis input and not a gap-fill.
entries.authority: C-02 and Phase 1 exit criterion 6, remediation spec 2026-08-01

entries.statement: The published fsQCA is not a calibration of the published axes. Five independent violations are recorded as D-103: identical raw values with divergent fuzzy membership, an inverted order between GBR and DEU on WSE, a near-constant condition present in every sufficient path, solution statistics that are internally inconsistent, and an outcome variable that contradicts the index it is meant to explain.
entries.effect: Pathway memberships, solution statistics and necessity results in vintages through v8.4 are not derived from the axes published beside them. The reported consistency of 1.000 on all three paths is an artefact of the near-constant condition, not a result.
entries.remedy: Re-run complete, and the necessity claim is no longer withheld pending a computation. The computation was run and the claim did not survive it. REE returns necessity consistency 0.7033 with Relevance of Necessity 0.5766 and coverage of necessity 0.5763, holds above 0.5 in 29 of 32 cases, and scores 0.7268 against the negated outcome, which is higher than it scores against the outcome itself. The gate returns TRIVIAL. Publish the four measures rather than a bare consistency figure, and withdraw the necessity claim rather than restating it at a lower number.
entries.supersedes_note: Through v8.3 this entry read as affecting only the HYPER condition's calibration against the ordinal ODI. That understated it: HYPER is one of five violations and not the most serious. Through v8.4 the claim was described as withheld pending a re-run, which invited the reading that a number was still owed. No number is owed. See errata D-103.
entries.authority: D-103, remediation spec 2026-08-01; necessity gate added 2026-08-01 (Relevance of Necessity, coverage of necessity, prevalence, negated outcome)

entries.statement: Fidelity is computed for 3 of 35 states (DEU, ESP, GBR).
entries.effect: Structural Lack is unavailable for the rest of the sample, so no fidelity ranking exists.
entries.remedy: Extend the Bhattacharyya computation to the full sample or state the three-state scope wherever fidelity is cited.

entries.statement: Availability-zone counts are missing for 27 of 35 states, so the ODI Herfindahl is weighted one unit per active cloud region rather than by capacity.
entries.effect: Operator concentration is measured by region count, which treats a one-zone and a six-zone region alike.
entries.remedy: Complete intra_region_fault_domains in cloud_regions_master.csv; the capacity-weighted value is already published where the source records it.

entries.statement: FPE, ESE are published per state and enter no composite (D-044).
entries.effect: The headline number omits the only fully component-audited axis (ESE) and the platform-exposure axis (FPE).
entries.remedy: Derive a weight from something, or keep stating the exclusion wherever the composite is presented. Do not assert a weight.

entries.statement: No semiconductor axis exists. The February 2026 roadmap named semiconductor capacity as the Infrastructure Pillar. Scoped as a declared roadmap item, target vintage v9.0, 2026-12-31, contingent on identifying a 35-state fabrication-capacity source. Until that date the roadmap claim is stated as pending, not delivered.
entries.effect: Compute-fabrication dependency is unmeasured. The roadmap claim is scoped rather than unsupported: it carries a target vintage, a date and the condition that would let it ship.
entries.remedy: Identify a 35-state fabrication-capacity source before 2026-12-31 and derive a weight, or record the item as retired on that date. An undated roadmap item is indistinguishable from an abandoned one.

entries.statement: The v8.0 ordinal ODI carried four manual overrides (NLD, HKG, KOR, SGP), each one step below its own stated rule, recorded in no export.
entries.effect: Any analysis reproducing the v8.0 ODI from its documented rule will disagree on those four states.
entries.remedy: Superseded by D-045. Retained here so the v8.0 discrepancy is explainable rather than mysterious.

entries.statement: CSE composes EMODnet and SubmarineMap at 0.6/0.4 for EU states and uses SubmarineMap alone elsewhere.
entries.effect: The axis is not constructed identically inside and outside the EU, so cross-region CSE comparisons carry a method difference.
entries.remedy: State the split wherever CSE is compared across regions.

coupling.exclusion_rule: The global matrix requires a complete vector over the six coupling axes. The states omitted are exactly those carrying a BIG coverage flag, not a discretionary selection.
coupling.interpretation: Substrate entanglement is geopolitical, not universal: energy-rich states decouple via cheap, reliable, carbon-heavy power; coupling concentrates in the import-dependent core.
coupling.derivation: Recomputed at build time from the published axes. rho = C/6 trace-normalised; CR = 1 - S(rho)/ln 6. Implementation verified against the published v8.0 values before use.
coupling.change_note: ODI now carries the continuous Herfindahl measure, so these correlations differ from the v8.0 published block, which was computed on the ordinal proxy. v8.0 reported global CR 0.11 and core 0.163.
coupling.construct_validity_warning: The FPE-ODI cell is definitional (FPE is 0.6*HHI, ODI is 100*HHI). Independent-measurement axes are WSE, CSE, REE and ESE only; their intercorrelations are the interpretable structure.

fsqca.model: WSE, CABLE, REE, HYPER, ESC_inv, GCI_inv -> HIGH_SOV_VULN (n=32; freq>=1; incl>=0.80; conservative; one absorption pass)

conditions_source.note: Both previously unqueryable (gap G2); exposed from v8.1.

fsqca.outcome_derivation: Calibrated from the published composite. The v6.6 outcome was not derived from the index it was meant to explain and gave DEU, ESP and GBR one shared value of 0.99 (D-103 violation E).

calibration.rule: Ragin direct method, two-sided logistic, sample percentiles 80/50/20
calibration.declared_because: The terms are anchor-sensitive. A sensitivity run at fixed 75/50/25 reproduces the v6.6 trivial-driver failure through REE, so anchors are part of the result rather than a setting.

sample.exclusion_rule: States withheld under BIG carry no composite and are excluded, never imputed (D-007). Causes are published under withholding_causes.

solution.pri_note: PRI is published beside raw consistency per path because the two diverge exactly where the result is weakest. A large gap means the path is consistent with the outcome and with its negation at once, which is a simultaneous subset relation rather than a finding. PRI below 0.50 disqualifies a path; 0.75 is the working convention.

intermediate.reason: No directional expectations declared. An intermediate solution is the complex solution plus the logical remainders that theory says are plausible, so it cannot be computed without that theory. Declare directional_expectations per condition to produce it.

coverage_ordering.note: Two-term check only: no intermediate solution was produced, because no directional expectations were declared.

solution.limit: The complex and parsimonious solutions are computed. The intermediate solution is not, because it requires declared directional expectations, which are a theoretical input rather than a computed one. Defaulting them would publish a theoretical claim as a result.
solution.v6_6_reporting_error: v6.6 reported intermediate 0.920 against parsimonious 0.76. Coverage cannot fall as logical remainders are added, because each solution is a superset of the one below it, so no single truth table can produce that pair. It is a reporting error. The assertion that catches it is now in the pipeline and holds on this run: parsimonious 0.7032 against complex 0.5807.

erratum.why_not_threshold: Under the sensitivity anchors REE returns consistency_N 0.9672, which is above 0.90. A withdrawal grounded on the 0.90 bar would be reversible by citing that regime. The disqualifying measure is Relevance of Necessity, below the 0.60 publishable bar under both regimes: 0.5766 primary and 0.195 sensitivity.
erratum.counterproof_negated_outcome: REE returns necessity consistency 0.727 against the negated outcome against 0.703 against the outcome, so it tracks the absence of the result more closely than the result. Under the sensitivity anchors it is necessary for the outcome and its negation alike, which discriminates nothing.
erratum.prevalence: Above the crossover in 29 of 32 cases under the primary anchors and 32 of 32 under the sensitivity anchors: a near-universal baseline state.
erratum.authority: Schneider, C. Q., and Wagemann, C. (2012), ch. 5.
erratum.note: PRI is a sufficiency measure and is not evidence for or against necessity. It appears in this block only under solution.per_path.

~WSE.reading: ~WSE scores 0.8092 against the negated outcome against 0.3449 against the outcome, so it tracks the negation at least as closely as the result. Neither figure is evidence of necessity. Report as trivial.

REE.reading: REE scores 0.7268 against the negated outcome against 0.7033 against the outcome, so it tracks the negation at least as closely as the result. Neither figure is evidence of necessity. Report as trivial.

~REE.reading: Publishable as necessary, with the prevalence caveat: ~REE holds above 0.5 in 3 of 32 cases (0.0938).

HYPER.reading: RoN 0.707 clears the bar but coverage of necessity 0.5979 is below 0.6. Report the value and decline the necessity label.

~HYPER.reading: ~HYPER scores 0.5752 against the negated outcome against 0.4979 against the outcome, so it tracks the negation at least as closely as the result. Neither figure is evidence of necessity. Report as trivial.

ESC_inv.reading: Publishable as necessary, with the prevalence caveat: ESC_inv holds above 0.5 in 16 of 32 cases (0.5).

~ESC_inv.reading: ~ESC_inv scores 0.6617 against the negated outcome against 0.5146 against the outcome, so it tracks the negation at least as closely as the result. Neither figure is evidence of necessity. Report as trivial.

GCI_inv.reading: GCI_inv scores 0.6033 against the negated outcome against 0.454 against the outcome, so it tracks the negation at least as closely as the result. Neither figure is evidence of necessity. Report as trivial.

~GCI_inv.reading: Publishable as necessary, with the prevalence caveat: ~GCI_inv holds above 0.5 in 16 of 32 cases (0.5).

fsqca.necessity_gate_method: Consistency alone cannot establish necessity: a condition held by almost every case is a superset of almost every outcome and scores high without carrying information. Four measures are published per condition and per negation: consistency_N, coverage_N as sum(min(X,Y))/sum(X), Relevance of Necessity as sum(1-X)/sum(1-min(X,Y)), and the count of cases holding the condition above 0.5. Necessity is re-run against the negated outcome, because a condition that tracks a result and its absence equally well discriminates nothing. Decision rule: RoN at or above 0.60 with coverage_N at or above 0.60 is publishable as necessary with the prevalence caveat; RoN below 0.50 is reported as non-necessary or trivial; between the two the value is reported and the necessity label declined.
fsqca.necessity_verdict: No condition or negation is publishable as necessary. REE, published at 0.916 in thesis section 4.5, returns consistency 0.703 under the primary anchors with RoN 0.577 and coverage_N 0.576, and it holds above 0.5 in 29 of 32 cases. It also scores 0.727 against the negated outcome, higher than the 0.703 it scores against the outcome, so it tracks the absence of the result more closely than the result. The gate returns TRIVIAL. The sensitivity run is the demonstration: under fixed 75/50/25 anchors REE's necessity consistency rises to 0.967, close to the published 0.916, while RoN falls to 0.195 and coverage_N to 0.389. The consistency figure rises precisely because the condition becomes near-constant, which is the artefact the bare number cannot show.

diagnostics.why_published: A condition that is high almost everywhere and present in every path yields consistency 1.000 trivially. Publishing the diagnostic is what lets a reader separate a result from an artefact.

sensitivity.finding: REE becomes near-constant and appears in every sufficient path, which is structurally the v6.6 failure arriving through a different condition.

robustness.status: PARTIAL. Sensitivity ranges implemented; the two robustness families below are declared and not yet computed.

sensitivity_ranges.what: Vary the calibration anchors, the raw consistency threshold and the frequency threshold, and report the range over which the solution holds rather than one point estimate.
sensitivity_ranges.evidence: Two anchor regimes are run: sample percentiles 80/50/20 as primary and fixed substantive 75/50/25 as sensitivity. They disagree, and the disagreement is the finding: REE becomes near-constant under the fixed anchors and its necessity consistency rises from 0.703 to 0.967 while RoN falls from 0.577 to 0.195.

fit_oriented_robustness.what: Compare parameters of fit across the test solutions: consistency, coverage and PRI under each perturbation, and report whether the solution's fit degrades gracefully or collapses.

case_oriented_robustness.what: Compare which cases are typical, deviant consistency and deviant coverage across the test solutions. A solution whose fit survives while its case membership churns is not robust in the sense that matters for interpretation.

not_to_be_confused_with.model_specification_robustness: The 6-condition to 7-condition respecification, published in vintages through v8.4 as `robustness_7cond`, is MODEL-SPECIFICATION robustness: it asks whether the result survives a different condition set. The Oana and Schneider protocol asks whether the result survives different analytic choices on one specification. They answer different questions and neither substitutes for the other. Labelling the respecification as the robustness protocol would overstate what was tested.

conceptual_independence_test.status: AD HOC. Not an established named procedure and not to be cited as one.
conceptual_independence_test.what_it_does: Re-runs the analysis against a variant outcome that is not derived from the composite, and reports how far the solution deflates. Through v8.3 this was recorded as `anticircularity: variant outcome deflates solution to 0.708`.
conceptual_independence_test.why_renamed: The former name implied a standard test with an accepted specification and an accepted threshold. There is neither. It is a conceptual-independence probe devised for this study, it is useful, and it carries no external authority. Citing it as an established procedure would borrow authority it does not have.
conceptual_independence_test.standing_limitation: The outcome is calibrated from the published composite, so the analysis explains the index using the axes the index is built from. That is coherent and it is circular, and the chapter states it plainly rather than resolving it with a test name.

recalibration_required.label_outcome: The re-run completed and the necessity label is declined. HYPER returns RoN 0.707 with coverage_N 0.598 under the primary anchors and RoN 0.756 with coverage_N 0.547 under the sensitivity anchors: consistency_N 0.584 and 0.650 respectively, both far below any necessity bar. Executing the instruction is not the same as recovering the claim.
recalibration_required.supersedes: The v8.4 block scoped this to the HYPER condition alone, which understated D-103 exactly as ledger entry U-02 did.
recalibration_required.scope_as_found: All six conditions and the outcome, per D-103 violations A to E.
recalibration_required.resolution: Full re-run against the published axes with every anchor re-derived. Reproduce with scripts/rerun_fsqca_d103.py in sovereign-infra.

fsqca.supersedes_pathways: The five v8.4 pathways were carried from the v6.6 calibration and are withdrawn. Pathway membership from any vintage at or before v8.4 is not citable.

fidelity.method: Bhattacharyya fidelity between trace-normalised stress distributions; Structural Lack = 1-F

sources: World Bank IC.ELC.OUTG SAIDI + ENTSO-E ERAA

odi_method.ordinal: 100*(4-n_providers)/3, a 4-level count proxy. v8.0 legacy, retained per country under audit.ODI_ordinal_value. Carried four manual overrides (NLD, HKG, KOR, SGP) that appear in no export.
odi_method.continuous: 100 * HHI over operator shares of active cloud regions per country. 35 of 35 states covered, spanning 25.6 to 100.0 against the four levels of the proxy.
odi_method.decision: D-045 resolved 2026-07-29: the composite and the coupling matrix consume the continuous measure. A macro polycrisis model runs time evolution and a Lindblad generator over these axes, and neither is defined on a step function.
odi_method.scale_note: The measures do not share a zero. Four evenly split operators give ordinal 0 but HHI 25, because four hyperscalers is concentration rather than its absence. Composites therefore rise slightly against v8.1; the shift is a scale change, not a data revision.
odi_method.limitation: ODI computes HHI over an UNWEIGHTED COUNT of active cloud regions (one unit per region), not over market shares. This is not the HHI of competition economics. AWS us-east-1 (6 AZs, dominant workload volume) contributes exactly one unit, identical to a single-AZ minor region. Capacity-weighted and AZ-weighted variants are not available (az_weighted_available: false). This limitation must be stated in the methods of any publication, not footnoted.
odi_method.prior_art: HHI-based cloud sovereignty measurement is not novel. Published Cloud Adoption Index constructions weight HHI supplier diversification at 40%; published EU cloud HHI estimates run 2500-3450. Any novelty claim must be narrowed to substrate-linked facility-level concentration and argued against this prior art.

derived_from.generator: v8.3 remediation transform T-1..T-5, F-11 applied to v8.2; see ops/VALIDATION_REPORT_CSOVE_AND_V83_2026-07-31.md
derived_from.note: Provenance transform. No axis value, composite or coverage figure changed, so the source hashes carried here remain the provenance of every number served in v8.4.

rgd_method.definition: RGD = 100*(n_regions-1)/(19-1). A min-max normalised count of active cloud regions, anchored on the USA at 19.
rgd_method.reason: D-049. The axis never measured reliance, workload or density. It is a normalised region count and is now named as one. The prior label invited a causal reading of an arithmetic quantity.
rgd_method.warning: RGD is algebraically coupled to ODI. ODI = 100*HHI over provider shares of the same regions, so ODI >= 100/n_providers >= 100/n_regions = 10000/(100+18*RGD). Any bivariate ODI-RGD result is bounded by this identity and must not be reported as an empirical relationship.

fpe_method.construction: FPE = 0.6*provider_concentration + 0.4*capex_exposure, where provider_concentration is the same HHI that defines ODI.
fpe_method.warning: FPE contains ODI as a 0.6-weighted component by construction. The reported coupling r(FPE,ODI)=0.783 is definitional, not empirical. FPE and ODI must never be interpreted as independent evidence of the same phenomenon.
fpe_method.status: diagnostic axis, excluded from the composite

csove_method.definition: CSovE_GAP = (CSovE_CLAIM + CSovE_VERIFY)/2. Claim-versus-verify epistemic gap on carbon.
sources: World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard Aug 2025
csove_method.coverage_finding: CSovE is sourced for 21 of 35 QESIS states. Coverage 0.60 is BELOW the BIG gate of 0.75. Under D-007 this is a finding, not a gap to fill. The source dataset covers a different 35-state population (14 states in CSovE are absent from QESIS; 14 QESIS states have no CSovE source document). The 14 unsourced states are correctly held NULL. No imputation was performed.
csove_method.status: DIAGNOSTIC AXIS. Excluded from the weighted composite.
csove_method.extended_formula_rejected: The source methodology proposes QESIS_EXTENDED = QESIS_Theory*0.88 + CSovE_GAP*0.12. REJECTED on two independent grounds. (1) Coverage 0.60 < 0.75 BIG gate. (2) On the 20 complete cases the correlation-ratio main effect of CSovE_GAP is 0.521 against a nominal weight of 0.12, a 4.3x inflation, which reproduces the nominal-versus-effective weight pathology documented in the 2026-07-31 audit. The source doc also states the weight is 'equivalent to CRD weight'; CRD/RGD nominal weight is 0.08, not 0.12.
csove_method.tier_defect_corrected: 9 of 21 published tier labels contradicted the stated boundaries and have been recomputed deterministically. The defect was a systematic boundary-rounding error.

effective_weights.method: Pearson correlation ratio (main effect Si), Paruolo, Saisana and Saltelli (2013), JRSS-A 176(3), 609-634. For a linear aggregation with approximately jointly normal inputs, Si = rho(Xi,Y)^2.

reduction_test.note: Deleting ODI, RGD and REE entirely (40% of nominal weight) leaves a ranking correlating at this level with the published one.

effective_weights.finding: Nominal and realised weights diverge. WSE realises roughly 1.8x its declared weight. ODI, RGD and REE together carry 40% of nominal weight and realise close to zero. REE is simultaneously quasi-necessary under fsQCA (consistency 0.916) and effectively weightless in the composite built from the same data.
effective_weights.honesty_caveat: At n=32 the bootstrap intervals are wide. Only WSE's inflation is distinguishable from its nominal weight at 95%. The point estimates for ODI, RGD and REE are near zero but their intervals do not exclude the nominal values. The defensible claim is that nominal weights are not identified at this sample size.

change_log_v8_3.change: CRD recomputed from v8.2 n_regions for all 35; 4 states corrected: HKG 11.1->5.6 (n_regions=2), KOR 16.7->5.6 (n_regions=2), NLD 5.6->0.0 (n_regions=1), SGP 16.7->11.1 (n_regions=3)
CRD renamed RGD across axes, composite_model and weights. rgd_method block added with the ODI coupling identity stated.
fpe_method block added; coupling matrix carries an explicit construct-validity warning.
odi_method carries the unweighted-count limitation and the prior-art constraint on novelty claims.
composites recomputed under corrected RGD; 2 changed: KOR 34.6->33.7, NLD 46.5->46.1
CSovE gated as diagnostic (coverage 0.60 < 0.75); EXTENDED formula rejected; 9 tier labels corrected.

approval.note: Approved by named human. No agent signed.

withholding_causes.note: The coverage arithmetic is what triggers the withholding. The cause explains why the coverage is missing and is not itself the trigger. Both are published because a reviewer told only the arithmetic cannot tell a measurement limit from a political one.

codes.SOURCE_RESOLUTION: The source measures at a resolution that does not resolve this territory. The value is absent for a measurement reason, and no amount of access would produce it.
codes.SOURCE_POLITICAL_COVERAGE: The source's territorial schema does not carry this entity as a separate entry. The value is absent for a coverage reason that is political in origin, not measurement error and not missing data.

withholding_causes.why_not_one_label: Recording all three as geopolitical data-accessibility exclusions would be accurate for Taiwan and wrong for Hong Kong and Singapore, whose absence is a catchment resolution limit that no access would resolve. One label over three different causes is the kind of claim a reviewer checks once and then distrusts throughout.

citation_concordance.why: Thesis figures and the served index now differ. A reader reproducing a published figure against this endpoint is told which vintage each number belongs to before concluding that the numbers are wrong. Under G-02 the served index is authoritative on any disagreement, and the published artefact is never silently retro-fitted.

errata.title: The QESIS Theory column is not the declared formula
errata.finding: The v6.6 sheet header declares WSE 0.30, CSE 0.30, ODI 0.17, CRD 0.08, REE 0.15. Recomputing that formula from the axis columns in the same sheet disagrees with the published column on 30 of 32 rows by more than 2 points. The deviation is sign-ordered: high-composite states inflated, low-composite states deflated. The column behaves as a rank-stretched transform, not a weighted sum.
errata.consequence: Every composite figure in the thesis derived from QESIS Theory is unciteable as a weighted index, including Germany at 17.5 and its rank of 34 of 35.
errata.action: The v6.6 and v8.0 composite is retired. Already done in the served index: v8.1 onward recomputes at build time. This record exists so the thesis figures stay explainable rather than mysterious.

errata.title: Missing WSE handled two contradictory ways
errata.finding: WSE is blank for HKG, SGP and TWN in v6.6. The resulting composites are HKG 75.2 at rank 6, TWN 75.2 at rank 6, and SGP 1.7 at rank 35. Identical missingness produced both the sixth-most-vulnerable and the least-vulnerable position in the sample. HKG and TWN additionally share a byte-identical composite and rank, which is a fill value rather than a computation.
errata.consequence: Any ranking of those three states in the thesis is an artefact of how the blank was filled, not a measurement.
errata.action: None needed in the served index: BIG withholds all three from v8.1 onward. This record justifies the withholding to a reviewer who asks why three states carry no composite.

errata.title: The fsQCA condition set is not a calibration of the published axes
errata.finding: Direct calibration is a monotonic transform of the raw value. Five results in the published set are impossible under it.

violations.detail: DEU and ESP both carry REE Stress 2026 of 91.5; fuzzy REE is 0.95 for DEU and 0.30 for ESP.
GBR carries WSE 26.0 with fuzzy 0.40; DEU carries WSE 40.8 with fuzzy 0.20. The UK has lower water stress than Germany and higher fuzzy membership.

ESC_inv across the sample: DEU 0.95, ESP 0.95, GBR 0.96, FRA 0.90, JPN 0.94, IND 0.942, POL 0.90, ITA 0.85. It appears in all three sufficient paths. A condition that is high almost everywhere and present in every path yields consistency 1.000 trivially. That is the mechanism behind the reported Consistency 1.000 and PRI 1.000 on all three paths: an artefact, not a result.

Reported intermediate coverage 0.920 against parsimonious coverage 0.76. The parsimonious solution uses all logical remainders and its raw coverage is normally at or above the intermediate. As reported the pair is internally inconsistent.

HIGH_SOV_VULN is 0.99 for DEU, ESP and GBR, identically. Germany's own composite ranks it 34 of 35, among the least vulnerable. The outcome variable is not derived from the index it is meant to explain, and the three narrative cases share one value.

errata.consequence: The fsQCA chapter must be re-run, not re-cited. Every necessity result, solution statistic and pathway membership in it is withdrawn pending that re-run.
errata.action: Supersedes uncertainty ledger entry U-02, which recorded this as affecting only the HYPER condition. U-02 is rewritten in this vintage to carry the full scope.

errata.title: Two headline numbers have no published method
errata.finding: The 27% figure is stated as EU AI Act compliance re-scored against three QESIS+ substrate axes, and which three is never specified. The claim that 36% of states face the risk of infrastructure collapse carries no threshold, no axis and no rule. Neither is reproducible.
errata.consequence: Both appear in three chapters and both carry rhetorical weight. A reader cannot check either one.
errata.action: Publish the rule, or withdraw the figures from the SSRN version. There is no third option that survives review.
errata.status: OPEN, author action on the SSRN deposit

errata.title: Figure 4.1 does not match its own caption
errata.finding: The caption states composite 17.5 and REE 91.5. The plotted bars are 86 and 12. Inverting on 100 minus x gives 82.5 and 8.5, not 86 and 12. The bars preserve the delta of 74 in the label while misstating both endpoints.
errata.status: OPEN, author action on the SSRN deposit

errata.title: Axis count and naming drift between thesis and index
errata.finding: Thesis §3.3 declares six axes: WSE, ESE, CSE, REE, CRD, ODI. The live index declares seven: WSE, CSE, REE, FPE, ODI, RGD, ESE. CRD at weight 0.08 in v6.6 was replaced by RGD at weight 0.08 in v8.3, the same slot carrying a different construct. FPE is the diagnostic descendant of CRD. Thesis Figure 4.4's caption reads Concentration of Resource Dependency while its own axis label reads Foreign Platform Exposure (FPE), so the published figure is already self-contradictory.
errata.action: The rename and the slot substitution are recorded here explicitly rather than left to be inferred from two documents that disagree.
